title: Tables & data — where it stands
eyebrow: Capability positioning · read from the source, not from memory
thesis: One enormous unified class — 2,517 methods, eleven sibling caps merged into a single `stzTable` — with engine-backed sort, aggregates, calculated columns, describe and pivot, plus a distinctive multi-table "TableX" pattern-query language. But measured against pandas, Polars and DuckDB it has three real holes: there is no join at all; group-by and filter run Ring-side even though engine bridges for both sit exported-but-unused; and the columnar engine is used per-operation, not as the live store. Ambition is pandas-eager, well short of Polars / DuckDB's vectorized columnar execution.
grid_title: Twelve lanes, each against its category leader
grid_lede: Every lane names what actually ships, the tools it is fair to measure against, and the one thing still owed. A recurring pattern here: an engine capability exists but the Ring face doesn't call it — so several lanes are rated on the Ring path that actually runs, not the dark engine bridge.

lanes.engine: `AddCalculatedCol` with an `@(:ColName)` formula, lowered engine-first through `StzEngineListEvalRows` — compile-once over all rows, with a Ring `eval()` fallback for non-arithmetic formulas. Guarded at 50k rows, chained calc columns and insert-position semantics.
lanes.owed: The one lane with measured engine scale. Short of Polars' fully-lazy vectorized expressions, but genuinely engine-backed and well-guarded.

lanes.engine: `SortOn(col)` ascending or descending via `StzEngineTableSortOn` → `table.zig sortOnColumn`: an index-permutation `std.sort.pdq` that moves companion columns without copying row objects, plus `IsSorted` predicates.
lanes.owed: A clean, copy-free engine sort — at parity for the operation. Multi-key stable sort with mixed asc/desc per key would round it out.

lanes.engine: Build from list-of-columns or hashlist; round-trip CSV (with separator control), JSON, and HTML tables (`FromHtml` / `ToHtmlXT`); SQLite via `stzDatabase` over the vendored engine.
lanes.owed: No Parquet / Arrow / Excel, the formats a modern data library lives on. And two rough edges: `FromJson` is marked `#TODO Test it`, and the CSV `iscsv` guards fail on a function-redefinition collision.

lanes.engine: Heterogeneous columns with per-column `type_hint` and per-cell tags (int/float/string/null) tracked in `table.zig`; `Cell`, `Row`, `Col`, `Section`, add/remove/rename column.
lanes.owed: Real typing, but many legacy access aliases (`colsection`, `rowz`, `cellsincol`, `cellatposition`) error after the 11→1 merge — the fidelity grind (see note) is exactly this surface.

lanes.engine: `Filter(paColValues)`, `FilterBy`, and predicate-string `FilterW` / `FilterWXT`, plus column projection. Multi-table querying via the TableX pattern language over `stzListOfTables`.
lanes.owed: The whole lane is Ring-side — the engine's `ring_FilterRows` exists but is never called — so filtering doesn't ride the columnar engine and won't vectorize.

lanes.engine: `stzPivotTable` + `stzPivotTableShow` for multi-dimension pivots and crosstabs, engine-backed via `StzEnginePivotCrossTab` / `ring_PivotGroupBy`; plus `Transpose` variants.
lanes.owed: No melt / unpivot / wide↔long — the inverse of pivot that tidy-data workflows depend on. Pivot ships; the reshape family is half-present.

lanes.engine: `Describe()` over all numeric columns, engine-backed through `frame.zig` (`StzEngineFrameDescribeAll` = 8 stats/col: count, mean, median, stddev, min, max, Q1, Q3) plus whole-table regression (`StzEngineFrameRegression`).
lanes.owed: Solid and engine-backed. The deeper statistical work (tests, distributions) lives on the Statistics page via `stzDataSet` — a separate, single-variable analyzer.

lanes.engine: Eleven caps (cell/column/row access, structure, subset, search, finder, sorter, replacer, aggregator, display) merged into one `stzTable` namespace, so any method reaches any other; the old classes survive as ~1 KB shells. A distinctive TableX pattern language queries collections of tables.
lanes.owed: The merge is sound engineering, but it left the legacy method surface unreconciled (150 erroring tests), and TableX is Ring-side and niche next to a real query language.

lanes.engine: Column reductions are engine-backed: `StzEngineTableSumCol` / `AvgCol` / `MinCol` / `MaxCol` / `ProductCol` / `CountNonNull` — cache-friendly columnar scans.
lanes.owed: Scalar-per-column aggregation is fast and correct; the gap is grouped aggregation (lane 10), where the engine path exists but the Ring `GroupBy` doesn't use it.

lanes.engine: `GroupBy(cols)` / `GroupByXT` exist and work — but as pure Ring row-wise hash-string keying.
lanes.owed: The engine already ships `groupByAggregate` (`table.zig`, `ring_GroupBy`) with O(n) hashed keys — but stzTable never calls it. The Ring path won't scale to the sizes Polars/DuckDB target.

lanes.engine: Null awareness exists — per-cell null tags, `AllItemsAreNull`, `CountNonNull`, and TableX null checks.
lanes.owed: No fillna / dropna / interpolate / forward-fill family — the everyday missing-data toolkit. Nulls can be detected but not systematically repaired or removed.

lanes.engine: A real columnar engine exists (`table.zig` — contiguous per-column arrays, copy-free sort, O(n) grouping), and SQL is available through `stzDatabase` over vendored SQLite.
lanes.owed: The Ring table keeps a row-wise `@aContent` and marshals the whole content per operation — the columnar engine is a per-op accelerator, not the live store. No query planner, no lazy execution; SQL is SQLite passthrough, not an in-house engine.

gaps_title: The gaps, ordered by return — not by size
gaps_lede: Three tiers. The first closes the two biggest capability holes — one of which is mostly a wiring job; the second pays down debt and everyday breadth; the third is the columnar ambition that would move it toward Polars/DuckDB.

items.title: Add joins
items.text: Inner, left, outer and cross joins — there is no join anywhere in the tables lane today, the single largest gap for a data-frame library. The columnar engine could host it; nothing does yet.

items.title: Wire group-by & filter to the engine
items.text: `ring_GroupBy` / `groupByAggregate` and `ring_FilterRows` are already compiled and exported — stzTable just doesn't call them. Routing the Ring paths to the existing engine bridges is high leverage for near-zero new engine code.

items.title: Finish the 11→1 fidelity grind
items.text: 150 of 251 legacy table tests error, almost all `R14` for method names not carried into the merged class. Reconciling them turns the advertised access surface from claimed into guarded — and the curated suites are already green to build on.

items.title: Missing-data toolkit + melt
items.text: A `fillna` / `dropna` / interpolate family and a `melt` / unpivot to complete the reshape lane — the tidy-data operations every workflow reaches for.

items.title: Fix the I/O rough edges
items.text: Test and confirm `FromJson` (currently `#TODO`), and resolve the CSV `iscsv` function-redefinition collision that fails those guards.

items.title: Make the columnar engine the live store
items.text: Stop marshalling row-wise `@aContent` per operation; hold data column-wise in the engine and run filter / group-by / join vectorized through it. This is the step from pandas-eager toward Polars/DuckDB execution.

items.title: Parquet & Arrow I/O
items.text: The formats a modern data library is expected to read and write, and the interchange layer that connects it to the rest of the ecosystem.

items.title: An in-house relational query surface
items.text: A query layer over `stzTable` itself (select/where/join/group as one planned expression), beyond today's SQLite passthrough — so relational queries run on the library's own columnar engine.

notes.lead: The honesty line on the ratings.
notes.text: The curated suites are green — `test_table_*` (core / access / aggregate / search / structure / engine-delegation) plus narrated calc-column, aggregation and regression guards (~90+ assertions) — and the lane ratings rest on those. The legacy numbered suite is not: 150 of 251 files error, overwhelmingly renamed methods from the 11→1 merge. And several lanes are rated on the Ring path that runs, not the engine bridge that exists but is never called (group-by, filter).

Softanza's tables are a broad, unified, partly engine-backed data-frame with a distinctive multi-table pattern language — competent for construct / sort / aggregate / pivot / describe — but they are not yet a pandas replacement, let alone a Polars/DuckDB one: no join, a Ring-side group-by, and a columnar engine that accelerates operations rather than owning the data.

footer: Read from the source on 2026-09-16 — Ring faces under `base/table` (`stzTable.ring` ~2,517 defs, the 11 merged caps, `stzPivotTable`, `stzListOfTables`) and `base/data` (`stzDatabase`); engine `table.zig` (columnar), `frame.zig` (describe/regression), `db.zig` (SQLite), `ring_bridge_table.zig`; connector `base/file/stzCSV.ring`; guards under `test/table` + `test/csv` + `test/database`. Ratings reflect what the guards prove.
